usageNotes: Use this to inspect which network interfaces on a specific node are participating in an SDN fabric and what their current link state and topology role are. The caller needs SDN.Audit permission on /sdn/fabrics/{fabric}; the target node must be online and the fabric must already exist. Results are node-local — run the same call against each cluster node to get a full fabric-wide picture.

examples.summary: List all interfaces on node 'pve1' that belong to the fabric 'evpn01'

tips: fabric id must be 2–8 alphanumeric characters and cannot start or end with a hyphen.
The 'type' field distinguishes Point-to-Point underlay links from Broadcast segments — useful when diagnosing OSPF/BGP neighborship issues.
An interface in 'down' state while the fabric is otherwise healthy usually indicates a physical or VLAN misconfiguration on that specific node.
This endpoint is node-scoped; iterate over all nodes in the cluster to build a complete interface-to-fabric map.
